title: Open problem on queue-number of bounded layered treewidth graphs
statement_text: It is open whether graphs of bounded layered treewidth have bounded queue-number.
context_text: A layering of a graph $G$ is a partition $(V_0,V_1,\dots,V_t)$ of $V(G)$ such that for every edge $vw$ with $v\in V_i$ and $w\in V_j$ we have $|i-j|\le 1$ (e.g. the BFS layering from a vertex). The layered width of a tree decomposition $(B_x:x\in V(T))$ of $G$ is the minimum $\ell$ such that, for some layering of $G$, each bag $B_x$ contains at most $\ell$ vertices of each layer; the layered treewidth of $G$ is the minimum layered width of a tree decomposition of $G$ (layered pathwidth is defined in the same way with path decompositions). A class has bounded layered treewidth if some constant bounds the layered treewidth of all its members. The queue-number of $G$ is the minimum $k$ such that there is a linear ordering of $V(G)$ and a partition of $E(G)$ into $k$ queues, i.e. sets of edges no two of which are nested (no edges $ab$, $cd$ with $a<c<d<b$ in the ordering). Planar graphs have layered treewidth at most 3, graphs of Euler genus $g$ at most $2g+3$, and graphs drawable on a surface of Euler genus $g$ with at most $k$ crossings per edge at most $2(2g+3)(k+1)$, so bounded layered treewidth allows arbitrarily large clique minors. Dujmović, Morin and Wood proved that every $n$-vertex graph with layered treewidth $k$ has track- and queue-number $O(k\log n)$, while graphs of layered pathwidth $k$ have queue-number at most $3k$. In a footnote the authors remark that, subsequent to the submission of this paper, improved bounds on the queue-number have been obtained (by Dujmović, Joret, Micek, Morin, Ueckerdt and Wood, who showed that planar graphs have bounded queue-number), but that it is still open whether all graphs of bounded layered treewidth have bounded queue-number.
